brief.headline: Aluminium settled higher and its backwardation more than doubled on a day when every other LME base metal fell - the tightness is aluminium's own, not the market's.
bullets: WHAT MOVED: on the 14-September LME official, aluminium cash settled $3,311.00, up $37.00 or 1.13%, and three-month $3,257.00, up just $7.00 or 0.22%. Copper, zinc, lead and nickel all fell on the same board. Warehouse stock slipped another 250 tonnes to 243,850 and the cash-to-three-month backwardation widened from $24.00 to $54.00.

WHY IT MATTERS: cash rose five times faster than three-month, which means the bid is for metal you can have now rather than metal in three months. Combine that with falling warehouse stock and a peer group that fell on the same session and the explanation is physical scarcity in the nearby market, not a macro re-rating of industrial metals.

THE COUNTERWEIGHT: the dollar is firming into a Federal Reserve decision on Wednesday where traders are now betting on a rate HIKE, not a cut, after hot August US inflation. The metal rose INTO that headwind rather than because of a tailwind - but the forward curve has not agreed yet, with three-month still below the 3,261 level it lost on Friday.

WHAT TO WATCH: Wednesday's central-bank decision, and whether three-month follows cash higher or the backwardation flattens again. A separate public disclosure on 14-September put the US Midwest premium at $1.09 a pound, off a June record, while the Asian quarterly benchmark is being negotiated 18-28% lower - so regional physical markets are moving in genuinely different directions and should not be read as one.

kpis.label: LME Cash settlement
kpis.note: THE WINDOW ROLLED AND THE NUMBER MOVED THE RIGHT WAY. LME ALUMINIUM CASH SETTLED $3,311.00 ON 14-SEPTEMBER, UP $37.00 OR +1.13% FROM FRIDAY'S $3,274.00, RECOVERING JUST OVER HALF OF FRIDAY'S $69.00 FALL. THE BOARD IS THE COMPLETE, PUBLISHED LME OFFICIAL FOR MONDAY 14-SEPTEMBER-2026. This page compiles at about 05:40 London on Tuesday 15-September, before today's 13:20 ring, so the latest published official belongs to the PRIOR session and that is stated rather than left to the date field. THE SESSION WAS VERIFIED IN BOTH LANGUAGES: the English and German Westmetall overviews were re-requested cache-busted this morning and both carry 14-September, line for line identical across all six metals, all six stock lines and all three FX fixings. The whole board is on ONE UNIFORM SESSION. No intraday or unofficial figure has been used anywhere. THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT FACT ABOUT THIS PRINT IS NOT THE LEVEL, IT IS THE COMPANY IT KEPT: ALUMINIUM WAS THE ONLY BASE METAL ON THE LME BOARD TO RISE. Copper three-month fell 1.18%, zinc 1.63%, lead 1.24% and nickel 0.09%, while aluminium three-month rose 0.22% and cash rose 1.13%. A metal that rises while its entire peer group falls is not being carried by a macro bid - it is being bid for its own reasons, and the curve says what those reasons are. THE BACKWARDATION MORE THAN DOUBLED, FROM $24.00 TO $54.00, AND WAREHOUSE STOCK FELL AGAIN TO 243,850 TONNES. Cash rose five times faster than three-month. That is the signature of physical tightness at the front of the curve, not of a speculative or supply-risk premium being paid across the whole strip. YESTERDAY THIS PAGE PUBLISHED AN EXPLICIT WARNING THAT A HIGHER PRINT WITH A FLATTER BACKWARDATION WOULD BE 'BEARISH INFORMATION WEARING BULLISH CLOTHES'. THE OPPOSITE HAPPENED AND IT IS RECORDED AS SUCH: the price rose AND the backwardation widened, which is the confirming combination rather than the trap, and the warning is therefore retired rather than quietly dropped.

kpis.note: LME ALUMINIUM THREE-MONTH SETTLED $3,257.00 ON 14-SEPTEMBER, UP $7.00 OR +0.22% FROM $3,250.00. THE BOARD IS THE COMPLETE, PUBLISHED LME OFFICIAL FOR MONDAY 14-SEPTEMBER-2026. This page compiles at about 05:40 London on Tuesday 15-September, before today's 13:20 ring, so the latest published official belongs to the PRIOR session and that is stated rather than left to the date field. THE SESSION WAS VERIFIED IN BOTH LANGUAGES: the English and German Westmetall overviews were re-requested cache-busted this morning and both carry 14-September, line for line identical across all six metals, all six stock lines and all three FX fixings. The whole board is on ONE UNIFORM SESSION. No intraday or unofficial figure has been used anywhere. THE THREE-MONTH IS THE NUMBER MOST INDEXED CONTRACTS REFERENCE AND IT BARELY MOVED, WHICH IS THE DISCIPLINED READ OF TODAY'S BOARD: cash rose 1.13% and three-month rose 0.22%, so the recovery is concentrated almost entirely in nearby metal. IT REMAINS BELOW THE 3,261 PIVOT THIS PAGE HAS TRACKED SINCE EARLY SEPTEMBER - by $4.00, against $11.00 on Friday - so the pivot is still contested rather than reclaimed, and it is not reported as reclaimed. The prior-month (August-2026) mean of $3,251.22 sits $5.78 below today's settlement, so the three-month is now marginally above its August average after spending Friday below it.

kpis.label: Cash-3M spread
kpis.note: THE CASH-3M SPREAD WIDENED FROM $24.00 TO $54.00 OF BACKWARDATION ON THE 14-SEPTEMBER OFFICIAL - THE BIGGEST SINGLE-SESSION WIDENING IN THE FIFTEEN-SESSION WINDOW ON THIS PAGE. CONVENTION, STATED SO THE SIGN IS NEVER AMBIGUOUS: cash above three-month is BACKWARDATION and indicates nearby tightness; cash below three-month is CONTANGO. Cash $3,311.00 against three-month $3,257.00 is therefore a $54.00 backwardation, and it has been in backwardation on every session in this window. THE SPREAD AND THE FLAT PRICE MOVED IN THE SAME DIRECTION TODAY, WHICH IS WORTH SAYING EXPLICITLY BECAUSE THEY DID NOT ON FRIDAY: on 11-September the flat price fell AND the backwardation narrowed, a coherent bearish pairing; on 14-September the flat price rose AND the backwardation widened by $30.00, a coherent bullish pairing. Two coherent sessions in a row in opposite directions is a market repricing nearby availability, not drifting. THE THREE-MONTH DID NOT CONFIRM WITH THE SAME CONVICTION, AND THAT LIMIT IS NOT HIDDEN: at $3,257.00 it is only $7.00 above Friday and still below the 3,261 pivot this page has tracked for a fortnight. THE FRONT OF THE CURVE IS TIGHTENING FASTER THAN THE FORWARD MARKET IS WILLING TO FOLLOW.

kpis.label: LME stocks (t)
kpis.note: LME WAREHOUSE STOCK FELL A FURTHER 250 TONNES TO 243,850 TONNES ON THE 14-SEPTEMBER REPORT, THE LOWEST LINE IN THE FIFTEEN-SESSION WINDOW ON THIS PAGE AND DOWN 3,075 TONNES OR 1.25% OVER THAT WINDOW. The draw is small in absolute terms and that is stated rather than dressed up - 250 tonnes is a rounding error against a 70-million-tonne market. WHAT MATTERS IS THE DIRECTION AND THE COMPANY IT KEEPS: stock has fallen on eight of the last fifteen sessions and risen on none, and it is falling while the backwardation is widening. Those two series are telling the same story and neither depends on the other for its evidence. PUBLIC CONTEXT FOR THE LEVEL, SOURCED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: a dated industry analysis published 15-September records that LME aluminium stocks fell 31.82% across the first half of 2026, attributing it to Russian sanctions and the Gulf crisis together; the commodity reference board describes LME inventories as close to a 36-year low. THE STOCK NUMBER ON THIS PAGE IS THEREFORE A LOW LEVEL STILL GRINDING LOWER, NOT A LOW LEVEL STABILISING.

kpis.label: EUR/USD (LME FX fixing)
kpis.note: EUR/USD FIXED AT 1.15480 ON THE 14-SEPTEMBER LME FX RATE, AGAINST 1.15920 ON 11-SEPTEMBER - THE EURO DOWN 0.38% AND THE DOLLAR CORRESPONDINGLY FIRMER. The ECB 14:15 fixing was 1.15510 from 1.15920 and the BFIX reference 1.15476 from 1.15916; all three fixings moved together, which is the internal-consistency check that a cached board would fail. A FIRMER DOLLAR IS A HEADWIND FOR A DOLLAR-PRICED METAL AND ALUMINIUM ROSE ANYWAY. That is the honest way to read today's print: the metal advanced INTO a macro headwind rather than on the back of a macro tailwind, which makes the physical explanation stronger rather than weaker. THE DOLLAR SIDE OF THIS IS NOT FINISHED: the commodity reference board captured this morning shows the dollar index at 99.60, up 0.12%, with traders adding to bets on a Federal Reserve RATE HIKE at Wednesday's decision after hot August US inflation. The euro leg of that trade has already moved; the metal leg has not.

lme.commentary: A NEW OFFICIAL PUBLISHED AND IT BROKE THE PATTERN OF THE PRECEDING WEEK. On 14-September LME aluminium cash settled $3,311.00 against $3,274.00, up $37.00 or +1.13%; three-month settled $3,257.00 against $3,250.00, up $7.00 or +0.22%; warehouse stock fell 250 tonnes to 243,850; and the cash-to-three-month backwardation widened from $24.00 to $54.00. THE BOARD IS THE COMPLETE, PUBLISHED LME OFFICIAL FOR MONDAY 14-SEPTEMBER-2026. This page compiles at about 05:40 London on Tuesday 15-September, before today's 13:20 ring, so the latest published official belongs to the PRIOR session and that is stated rather than left to the date field. THE SESSION WAS VERIFIED IN BOTH LANGUAGES: the English and German Westmetall overviews were re-requested cache-busted this morning and both carry 14-September, line for line identical across all six metals, all six stock lines and all three FX fixings. The whole board is on ONE UNIFORM SESSION. No intraday or unofficial figure has been used anywhere. THE STRUCTURE OF THE MOVE MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE. Cash rose five times faster than three-month, so the entire recovery is concentrated in nearby metal and almost none of it has been priced into the forward curve. THAT IS A PHYSICAL TIGHTNESS SIGNAL RATHER THAN A DIRECTIONAL ONE, and it is corroborated by the stock line falling on the same report to the lowest level in this fifteen-session window. THE CROSS-METAL EVIDENCE IS THE STRONGEST PART OF TODAY'S READ AND IT IS AVAILABLE ON THE SAME BOARD, ON THE SAME SESSION, FROM THE SAME SOURCE. Copper three-month fell 1.18% to $14,065.50, zinc fell 1.63% to $3,809.00, lead fell 1.24% to $1,873.50 and nickel fell 0.09% to $16,400.00. Aluminium was the only riser. A dollar-led risk-off session normally takes the whole complex down together, and it did - with one exception. THE EXCEPTION IS THE INFORMATION. WHAT HAS NOT HAPPENED IS ALSO REPORTED. The three-month is still $4.00 below the 3,261 pivot and $117.00 below the 3,374 upside trigger, so nothing on the technical panel has been confirmed. The move recovered a little over half of Friday's fall on cash and only a tenth of it on three-month. THE FORWARD MARKET HAS NOT AGREED WITH THE SPOT MARKET YET, and until it does this is a tightness print rather than a trend change. THE DAY'S HEADWINDS WERE REAL AND THE METAL ROSE THROUGH THEM: the LME euro fixing fell to 1.15480 from 1.15920, the dollar index is 99.60 and firming, and traders are adding to bets on a Federal Reserve rate HIKE on Wednesday. A dollar-priced metal that advances into a firming dollar on the day its peer group falls is doing something idiosyncratic, and the curve and the stock line both say what.

regional.basis: SETTLED QUARTERLY BENCHMARK, UNCHANGED AND UNCHANGEABLE UNTIL THE QUARTER TURNS. S&P Global Platts settled the July-September Japanese premium at a record $395/t CIF Japan, assessed 06-Jul-2026, up 12.4% on Q2-2026's $351.50/t. THE Q4 REPLACEMENT REMAINS PENDING AND THE RANGE ON THIS PAGE IS UNCHANGED AT $280-310. It was narrowed from $290-325 on 11-September when a dated consensus printed and it has not been narrowed since, because nothing newer has printed and a range is not tightened on repeated readings of the same evidence. THE DATED 12-SEPTEMBER CORROBORATION STANDS: Japanese buyers have been offered $310-325/t for October-December shipments, down 18-22% from the $395/t agreed for July-September, while a separate market consensus reported 11-September put the likely settlement at $280-290/t with Korean and Thai traders repricing toward that band. THE CONSENSUS SITS BELOW THE PRODUCERS' OWN OPENING OFFER, WHICH PUTS THE BURDEN OF CONCESSION ON THE SELLERS. A settlement at $285 would be a fall of roughly 28% from this record in a single quarter. NOTE THE TENSION WITH TODAY'S EXCHANGE BOARD AND DO NOT RESOLVE IT PREMATURELY: the LME curve tightened sharply on 14-September while the Asian premium negotiation is still pointing sharply lower. Those are different markets - warrant metal in a warehouse versus delivered metal in Japan - and they are allowed to disagree.

CARRIED AT ITS LAST DATED PUBLIC ASSESSMENT. NO NEWER DATED MARK PRINTED INTO THE 15-SEPTEMBER PRE-RING COMPILE WINDOW AND NOTHING HAS BEEN INTERPOLATED OR ESTIMATED. Premium assessments are PERIODIC rather than daily - quarterly benchmarks settle four times a year and spot assessments publish weekly or fortnightly - so the absence of a new mark on a given morning is expected rather than anomalous. It is stated on the row rather than left to the date field. THE STALENESS IS DIRECTIONALLY MISLEADING AND THAT IS WHY IT IS SPELLED OUT: every piece of dated commentary since this mark was assessed points to Asian spot premiums softening toward the $280-325 band now being discussed for the Q4 quarterly, so a carried $370 is more likely to be too HIGH than too low. It is carried anyway rather than adjusted, because adjusting an assessment without an assessment is fabrication. THE ONE NEW PIECE OF EVIDENCE THIS RUN CUTS THE OTHER WAY AND IS RECORDED FOR BALANCE: a public producer disclosure dated 14-September states that Middle East supply remains constrained by the war and that North American and European customers are actively seeking material. Asia is not named in that disclosure and no inference is drawn about it.

Premium assessments are PERIODIC rather than daily - quarterly benchmarks settle four times a year and spot assessments publish weekly or fortnightly - so the absence of a new mark on a given morning is expected rather than anomalous. It is stated on the row rather than left to the date field. THE EUROPEAN ROW HAS A DATED PIECE OF SUPPORTING EVIDENCE THIS RUN EVEN THOUGH ITS NUMBER HAS NOT MOVED. The European cost backdrop improved marginally on the same day: TTF gas eased 0.33% to about EUR 82.30/MWh after the previous session's 4.56% jump, which matters for European smelter economics far more than the crude price does.

CARRIED AT ITS LAST DATED PUBLIC ASSESSMENT. NO NEWER DATED MARK PRINTED INTO THE 15-SEPTEMBER PRE-RING COMPILE WINDOW AND NOTHING HAS BEEN INTERPOLATED OR ESTIMATED. Premium assessments are PERIODIC rather than daily - quarterly benchmarks settle four times a year and spot assessments publish weekly or fortnightly - so the absence of a new mark on a given morning is expected rather than anomalous. It is stated on the row rather than left to the date field. THIS ROW IS DELIBERATELY NOT UPDATED TO TODAY'S NEW US NUMBER AND THE REASON IS A BASIS DIFFERENCE RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. A new, dated, public US Midwest figure DID print on 14-September - about $2,403/t, $1.09 per pound - but it came from a producer executive speaking at an investor conference, NOT from the price reporting agency that settles this particular assessment. MIXING AN AGENCY ASSESSMENT SERIES WITH AN EXECUTIVE'S QUOTED LEVEL INSIDE ONE ROW WOULD CORRUPT THE SERIES, so the agency row is held at its last agency mark of $2,094/t and the newly sourced level is carried on the separate US Midwest Duty-Paid row below, where the source is stated on its face. THE DIVERGENCE BETWEEN THE TWO ROWS - $2,094 AGENCY-ASSESSED VERSUS $2,403 EXECUTIVE-QUOTED - IS THEREFORE VISIBLE ON THIS PAGE RATHER THAN AVERAGED AWAY, and readers should treat the gap as a measure of how uncertain the US premium print currently is rather than as an error.

UPDATED THIS RUN TO A NEW, DATED, PUBLIC MARK - THE FIRST MOVEMENT ON THE US PREMIUM PANEL IN DAYS. Speaking at the Jefferies Global Industrials Conference in New York on 14-SEPTEMBER-2026, Alcoa's chief financial officer stated that the Midwest premium 'currently stands at USD 1.09 per pound (USD 2,403 per tonne)', having eased from a record USD 1.19 per pound in June. THE SOURCE IS A NAMED EXECUTIVE AT A PUBLIC INVESTOR CONFERENCE, REPORTED BY TRADE PRESS - IT IS PUBLIC AND ATTRIBUTABLE, BUT IT IS NOT A PRICE-REPORTING-AGENCY ASSESSMENT, and that distinction is stated on the row rather than buried. The previous value of $2,094 shown in the change column is this page's prior carried agency-basis figure, so the +$309 move is PART REPRICING AND PART BASIS CHANGE and should not be read as a clean day-over-day premium move. THE SUBSTANCE OF THE DISCLOSURE MATTERS MORE THAN THE NUMBER. The executive argued that a cut in US tariffs on CANADIAN aluminium alone would not bring the premium down significantly, because the United States needs to import about 4 million tonnes a year while Canada can supply roughly 3 million - leaving about 1 million tonnes that must be incentivised from Japan, South Korea or Europe, where trade barriers continue to support delivered cost. Her stated conclusion: 'even if we were to have a favorable rate with Canada, we don't see Midwest dropping significantly. It might come off a little bit, but we wouldn't see it returning to pre-tariff levels.' SHE ALSO SET OUT THE CONDITION UNDER WHICH IT WOULD FALL HARD - broader tariff relief extended to Japan, Korea and Europe, in which case 'you can expect the Midwest premium to reduce in response to essentially wipe out the tariff benefit.' THAT IS THE CLEAREST PUBLICLY STATED TRIGGER CONDITION FOR THE US PREMIUM AVAILABLE ON THIS PAGE AND IT IS RECORDED VERBATIM RATHER THAN PARAPHRASED AWAY. DECOMPOSITION ON TODAY'S BOARD: at the verified 50% Section 232 rate applied to the 14-September cash settlement of $3,311.00, the tariff leg is $1,655.50, leaving an implied market leg of roughly $747.50 - about 31% of the delivered premium. THE TARIFF IS STILL THE MAJORITY OF THE US NUMBER.

drivers.text: THE US PREMIUM PANEL MOVED FOR THE FIRST TIME IN DAYS, ON A NAMED PUBLIC DISCLOSURE, AND THE NUMBER IS LOWER THAN THE RECORD BUT HIGHER THAN THIS PAGE WAS CARRYING — Speaking at the Jefferies Global Industrials Conference in New York on 14-September, Alcoa's chief financial officer put the US Midwest premium at USD 1.09 per pound - about USD 2,403 per tonne - down from a record USD 1.19 per pound in June. This page had been carrying $2,094/t on an agency assessment basis, so the change shown on the row is part genuine repricing and part basis change, and that is stated on the row rather than presented as a clean daily move. The disclosure is public, attributed and dated; it is not a price-reporting-agency assessment, and the two bases are kept on separate rows so neither series is corrupted.

drivers.text: THE CLEAREST PUBLICLY STATED TRIGGER CONDITION FOR A FALL IN THE US PREMIUM IS NOW ON THE RECORD, AND IT IS NOT THE ONE MOST COMMENTARY ASSUMES — The same executive said a cut in US tariffs on CANADIAN aluminium alone would not bring the Midwest premium down significantly, because the United States must import about 4 million tonnes a year while Canada can supply roughly 3 million - leaving about 1 million tonnes that has to be attracted from Japan, South Korea or Europe, where barriers keep delivered cost high. Her stated view: 'even if we were to have a favorable rate with Canada, we don't see Midwest dropping significantly.' The condition under which it WOULD fall hard is broader relief extended to those other suppliers, at which point, in her words, the premium would 'essentially wipe out the tariff benefit.' THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE IS THAT A CANADA HEADLINE IS NOT THE SIGNAL TO WATCH; A MULTI-COUNTRY RELIEF HEADLINE IS.

drivers.text: THE TARIFF LEG IS STILL THE MAJORITY OF THE US DELIVERED NUMBER AND THE DECOMPOSITION IS RECOMPUTED EVERY RUN AGAINST THE LIVE CASH SETTLEMENT — Section 232 is re-verified this run at 50% on aluminium articles and 25% on derivatives, with Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and the EU. Applied to the 14-September cash settlement of $3,311.00, the tariff leg of the US duty-paid number is $1,655.50, leaving an implied market leg of roughly $747.50 against the newly sourced $2,403/t - about 31% of the delivered premium. NOTE THAT THE TARIFF LEG ROSE $18.50 TODAY PURELY BECAUSE THE LME CASH PRICE ROSE, WITHOUT ANY POLICY CHANGE, which is an arithmetic artefact of an ad-valorem duty and is flagged so it is not read as a policy move. No freight, financing or tightness split is published because no public series supports one.
drivers.source: Westmetall - LME official cash settlement, 14-September-2026 board (both language versions agree)

drivers.text: THE PHYSICAL-SCARCITY PILLAR UNDER WESTERN PREMIUMS WAS CONFIRMED ON THE RECORD BY A PRODUCER ON THE SAME DAY THE LME CURVE CONFIRMED IT INDEPENDENTLY — Two unrelated pieces of evidence pointed the same way on 14-September. The exchange board showed cash rising 1.13% against three-month rising 0.22%, the backwardation widening from $24.00 to $54.00 and stock falling to 243,850 tonnes - all front-of-curve tightness. Separately and independently, a listed producer stated publicly that Middle East supply remains constrained by the war, that North American and European customers are actively seeking material, and that its order book is almost completely sold out for the remainder of 2026. A dated 15-September analysis adds that LME aluminium stocks fell 31.82% across the first half of 2026 on the combination of Russian sanctions and the Gulf crisis. THE COUNTERWEIGHT IS REGIONAL AND IS NOT SUPPRESSED: the Asian quarterly negotiation is still pointing 18-28% lower for Q4, so scarcity is not being priced uniformly across regions.
drivers.source: AL Circle, 15-September-2026 - H1'26 LME aluminium stocks dip 31.82%: Russian sanctions & Gulf crisis pack a double blow

prices.label: Bauxite (SMM imported index / Guinea CIF China)
prices.note: THE PRICE FIELD IS CARRIED AT ITS LAST DATED PUBLIC MARK AND NOTHING HAS BEEN INTERPOLATED, BUT THE FORWARD VIEW ON THIS ROW HAS BEEN REVISED DOWN THIS RUN ON DATED PUBLIC FORECASTS AND THE REVISION IS EXPLAINED. A 12-September industry analysis puts 2026 GUINEA FOB BAUXITE AT USD 34-46 PER DRY METRIC TONNE AGAINST USD 40-65 IN 2025, and AUSTRALIAN FOB AT USD 39.15 PER WET METRIC TONNE IN FY26 AGAINST USD 51.48 IN FY25. Guinean shipments reached 4.33 Mt in the 21-27 August week, up 3.7% week on week and 28.4% year on year, even as some suspended Guinean mines continued to stockpile at port with no near-term plan to resume. THE TREND FIELD IS THEREFORE MOVED FROM UP TO DOWN, AND THE ONE PIECE OF CONTRARY EVIDENCE IS KEPT VISIBLE RATHER THAN DROPPED: the 11-September Chinese port survey showed inventories across ten domestic ports falling 1,610,000 tonnes week on week, a large draw. THE TWO FACTS ARE RECONCILABLE - a refinery system running flat out consumes bauxite fast - BUT THE DRAW THINS THE BUFFER AGAINST A GUINEA INTERRUPTION, WHICH REMAINS THE MOST CONCENTRATED COUNTRY RISK ON THIS PAGE. Because roughly two tonnes of alumina are required per tonne of aluminium and two to three tonnes of bauxite per tonne of alumina, a bauxite disruption propagates through the chain with a lag rather than immediately.

THE 07-SEPTEMBER REPORTING THAT IRAN DESCRIBED A DEAL AS DAYS AWAY IS NOT DELETED AND WAS NOT WRONG - IT IS SUPERSEDED BY THE FACT THAT THE MEETING IT POINTED TO DID NOT HAPPEN. AND THE BYPASS IS NOW DOWN, WHICH IS THE MORE IMPORTANT HALF OF TODAY'S CHANGE: Saudi Arabia has suspended its East-West crude pipeline after Thursday's drone attacks with no restart date - around 7 million barrels a day of capacity to Red Sea ports and the principal route that routes AROUND this strait. A CHOKEPOINT WITHOUT A WORKING BYPASS IS A DIFFERENT RISK FROM A CHOKEPOINT WITH ONE. THE WATERWAY HAS NOT REOPENED, NOTHING HAS BEEN SIGNED, AND NO NEW MEETING DATE HAS BEEN PUBLISHED. Brent at a four-month high is the market's own vote on this row.

logistics.label: Red Sea / Bab al Mandeb corridor
logistics.note: A SECOND CHOKEPOINT REMAINS IN PLAY AND NOTHING PUBLISHED THIS WEEKEND CHANGED IT. The Houthi group was reported to have seized the port city of Mocha, gaining leverage over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, declaring a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia and striking Saudi energy infrastructure; Bab el-Mandeb transits are down about 24% since the July blockade and MARAD advisory 2026-006 runs to 22-September. THE IMPORTANCE IS ROUTING RATHER THAN VOLUME: Bab el-Mandeb is the alternative on which Hormuz-affected cargo has partly relied, so two contested chokepoints are not twice the risk of one - THEY REMOVE THE SUBSTITUTE. THAT LOGIC NOW RUNS IN REVERSE AND IT IS WORTH SAYING SO: if the Hormuz arrangement reported on 07-September completes, the pressure on Bab el-Mandeb as a substitute route falls at the same time, and the shipping-risk premium embedded in Western delivered prices unwinds from both ends at once. headlines.title: ALUMINIUM'S CASH-TO-THREE-MONTH BACKWARDATION MORE THAN DOUBLED ON THE 14-SEPTEMBER LME OFFICIAL, FROM $24.00 TO $54.00, AS CASH SETTLED $3,311.00 AGAINST THREE-MONTH $3,257.00. Cash rose 1.13% while three-month rose only 0.22%, so the entire recovery from Friday's fall is concentrated in nearby metal. Warehouse stock fell a further 250 tonnes to 243,850, the lowest line in the fifteen-session window carried on this page. A widening backwardation alongside a falling stock line is the textbook signature of physical tightness at the front of the curve, and the two series are independent of each other, which is why both are reported. THE FORWARD MARKET HAS NOT CONFIRMED: three-month remains $4.00 below the 3,261 pivot lost on Friday and $117.00 below the 3,374 upside trigger, so this is a tightness print rather than a trend change.

ALUMINIUM WAS THE ONLY BASE METAL TO RISE ON THE 14-SEPTEMBER LME BOARD. Copper three-month fell 1.18% to $14,065.50, zinc fell 1.63% to $3,809.00, lead fell 1.24% to $1,873.50 and nickel fell 0.09% to $16,400.00, while aluminium three-month rose 0.22% and cash rose 1.13%. The curve structures diverged just as sharply: copper sits in contango with cash $21.50 below three-month, while aluminium's backwardation widened to $54.00. A dollar-led session normally drags the whole complex down together and it did - with one exception. BECAUSE ALL FIVE METALS SHARE THE SAME MACRO ENVIRONMENT, THE SAME EXCHANGE, THE SAME SESSION AND THE SAME SOURCE, THE DIVERGENCE ISOLATES THE CAUSE: it is physical and it is aluminium's own.

THE US MIDWEST PREMIUM CURRENTLY STANDS AT USD 1.09 PER POUND, ABOUT USD 2,403 PER TONNE, DOWN FROM A RECORD USD 1.19 PER POUND IN JUNE, according to Alcoa's chief financial officer speaking at the Jefferies Global Industrials Conference in New York on 14-September. She argued that a cut in US tariffs on Canadian aluminium ALONE would not bring the premium down significantly, because the United States needs to import about 4 million tonnes a year while Canadian suppliers can provide roughly 3 million, leaving about 1 million tonnes that must be attracted from markets where trade barriers still support delivered cost. Her stated view: 'even if we were to have a favorable rate with Canada, we don't see Midwest dropping significantly. It might come off a little bit, but we wouldn't see it returning to pre-tariff levels.' THE CONDITION FOR A LARGER FALL IS BROADER RELIEF EXTENDED TO JAPAN, KOREA AND EUROPE, WHICH WOULD, IN HER WORDS, 'ESSENTIALLY WIPE OUT THE TARIFF BENEFIT'.

A LISTED PRODUCER STATED PUBLICLY ON 14-SEPTEMBER THAT MIDDLE EAST SUPPLY REMAINS CONSTRAINED BY THE WAR, THAT NORTH AMERICAN AND EUROPEAN CUSTOMERS ARE ACTIVELY SEEKING AVAILABLE MATERIAL, AND THAT ITS ORDER BOOK IS ALMOST COMPLETELY SOLD OUT FOR THE REMAINDER OF 2026. The same disclosure records that the company produces about 900,000 tonnes a year in Canada and pays more than USD 1 billion in tariffs on the majority of that metal shipped into the US, and that the elevated Midwest premium is 'fully compensating us for that, as well as returning as margin because of the tightness in tons'. THIS IS AN INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION OF THE SAME CONCLUSION THE LME CURVE REACHED ON THE SAME DAY, FROM A COMPLETELY DIFFERENT KIND OF EVIDENCE - a company order book rather than a warrant market.

LME ALUMINIUM STOCKS FELL 31.82% ACROSS THE FIRST HALF OF 2026, according to a dated 15-September industry analysis that attributes the draw to Russian sanctions and the Gulf crisis acting together - describing the two as a double blow that carried the LME price to four-year highs before it cooled. The commodity reference board separately describes LME inventories as close to a 36-year low and SHFE stockpiles as continuing to fall. THIS IS THE STRUCTURAL CONTEXT THAT MAKES A 250-TONNE DAILY DRAW WORTH REPORTING: the absolute daily number is trivial, but it is the continuation of a halving-scale move in available warrant metal over six months, and it is happening while the curve is backwardated.

TRADERS HAVE INCREASED BETS ON A FEDERAL RESERVE RATE HIKE AT WEDNESDAY 16-SEPTEMBER'S DECISION AFTER STUBBORNLY HOT US INFLATION, FIRMING THE DOLLAR AND WEIGHING ON DOLLAR-PRICED COMMODITIES. The dollar index stands at 99.60, up 0.12%, EUR/USD at about 1.1537, and the US ten-year yield at 5.013%, through the 5% handle. The market is pricing the probability of a HIKE rather than debating the size of a cut, which removes the monetary leg from every industrial-metal bull case at precisely the moment the physical market is tightening. A yield above 5% also raises the carrying cost of financed inventory, which discourages holding metal off-warrant. TWO FORCES ARE PULLING IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS AND WEDNESDAY IS WHEN ONE OF THEM RESOLVES.

A DATED 14-SEPTEMBER SHANGHAI METALS MARKET COMMENTARY READS THAT MACRO RATE-HIKE EXPECTATIONS ARE PRESSURING ALUMINIUM PRICES WHILE CHINA'S CONTINUED DESTOCKING UNDERPINS THE MARKET. A separate dated review records that Chinese aluminium extended its gains into August, with supply tightness and demand recovery expected to support September. The two-sided framing is the same one this page has carried for a week, now restated on the current session rather than on last week's. NO NEW DATED NUMERIC CHINESE MARK - no SHFE official, no SMM spot premium, no inventory tonnage - printed into this compile window, so no Chinese figure on this page has been changed and none has been estimated. The row is carried on direction, not on a number.

THE ESCALATING US-CANADA TARIFF DISPUTE IS PUTTING NORTH AMERICAN AUTO-PARTS SUPPLY CHAINS UNDER PRESSURE, per a dated 14-September report, with parts makers facing higher costs and growing uncertainty over where and how components should be produced across a network built over decades of integration. Canada's counter-tariffs have been in force since 08-September at 50% across USD 27.6bn of US goods. THE DEMAND-SIDE CONSEQUENCE IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS FOR METAL: automotive is one of the largest end-uses for both rolled and extruded aluminium in North America, and sustained uncertainty over component sourcing is a brake on order books regardless of where the metal itself is priced.

A BRITISH COLUMBIA ALUMINIUM EXTRUDER HAS PUBLICLY REFUSED TO RELOCATE PRODUCTION TO THE UNITED STATES DESPITE TARIFFS THAT COULD EFFECTIVELY SHUT IT OUT OF ONE OF ITS LARGEST MARKETS, in which more than 40% of its sales previously originated, per a dated 15-September report. THE ITEM IS CARRIED BECAUSE IT IS EVIDENCE ON A QUESTION THE TARIFF REGIME WAS EXPLICITLY DESIGNED TO ANSWER: whether duties actually relocate downstream capacity into the United States or simply destroy trade. A single company is not a data set and is not presented as one, but it is a dated, named, public counter-example to the reshoring assumption, and counter-examples are worth more than confirmations when the policy is this recent.

RUSAL IS NEARING THE FINAL STAGE OF PERMITTING FOR A BAUXITE-TO-ALUMINA PROCESSING PROJECT IN KALIMANTAN, INDONESIA, according to the Indonesian energy and mineral resources minister in a dated 14-September report. Separately and on the same date, Mercuria and Glencore are reported to be exploring a potential deal for Venezuela's Venalum smelter, the country's largest, which has spent years producing only a fraction of its original capacity. NEITHER ITEM CHANGES A 2026 BALANCE AND NEITHER IS TREATED AS IF IT DOES - refineries and smelter restarts run on multi-year clocks. They are logged because the capacity pipeline is the mechanism by which today's unusually wide smelter margins eventually close, and the pipeline is visibly lengthening in exactly the regions where energy is cheap.

BAUXITE SUPPLY IS RISING AND FORWARD PRICE FORECASTS HAVE BEEN CUT ON BOTH MAJOR ORIGINS, per a dated 12-September industry analysis carried unchanged because nothing newer has printed and nothing has contradicted it. Guinean shipments reached 4.33 Mt in the 21-27 August week, up 28.4% year on year, and Asia exported 7.05 Mt of alumina worth USD 2.76bn in H1-2026, up 27.36% year on year. THE FEEDSTOCK LAYER BENEATH THE SMELTER IS LOOSENING WHILE THE METAL ITSELF IS TIGHTENING, which is precisely the configuration that produces the very wide conversion margins the peer-earnings panel on this page has been reporting from company disclosures all quarter. The counterweight is that Chinese port bauxite inventories have been drawing down, so the loosening is not uniform across regions.

THE ENERGY COMPLEX DECELERATED AND THE GAS LEG REVERSED. Brent is about $106.96, up 1.21%, against the 2.86% gain this page reported yesterday, and WTI about $102.91, up 1.49%. European gas TTF EASED 0.33% to about EUR 82.30/MWh after jumping 4.56% in the previous session. THE GAS REVERSAL IS THE COMMERCIALLY IMPORTANT HALF, because power is 30-40% of primary aluminium cash cost and in Europe the marginal power price is set by gas far more often than by anything else. The underlying supply-route risk - postponed Hormuz corridor talks and the shut Saudi East-West bypass pipeline - has not been resolved, so this is a pause in the repricing rather than a resolution of it, and it is reported as a pause.

THE WORLD'S LARGEST ALUMINA PRODUCER EARNED MATERIALLY LESS IN A QUARTER WHEN THE LME CASH AVERAGE WAS ABOVE $3,200, AND THAT IS THE SIGNAL. A 26% year-on-year fall in Q2 attributable profit on flat-to-lower revenue points to margin compression rather than volume weakness, and it is consistent with the Chinese alumina spot picture carried on this board - SMM's Shandong index down toward 2,600 RMB/t with national capacity utilisation rising and trader inventories building. For a reader of the seaborne market the implication runs both ways: weaker Chinese alumina margins are disinflationary for the smelter cost basket globally, but a large integrated producer earning less at a high metal price also argues that the cost curve has moved up underneath everyone. The shares fell around 3% on the release. earnings.note: STRONGEST QUARTER OF THE YEAR AT THE DOWNSTREAM END OF THE CHAIN. Fourth-quarter FY26 revenue rose 25.2% year-on-year to MYR 204.8 million (USD 50.8 million) from MYR 163.5 million (USD 40.5 million), on higher sales volumes in the group's extrusion and fabrication segment; the company reports its strongest quarterly revenue and profit of the financial year, with the headline putting quarterly profit up about 200% to roughly USD 4.5 million. The result funds a MYR 100 million (USD 24.8 million) expansion plan and a diversification away from its core solar-sector business. FIGURES ARE TAKEN FROM THE PUBLIC REPORT AS PUBLISHED; the full profit-and-loss detail below the revenue line was truncated in the public summary and nothing is inferred to fill it. A USEFUL COUNTERWEIGHT TO THE CHINESE DOWNSTREAM PICTURE RATHER THAN A CONTRADICTION OF IT, AND THE DISTINCTION IS GEOGRAPHIC. SMM's 24-August daily describes Chinese downstream processing operating rates as under pressure with pre-peak-season stockpiling absent, and Chinese billet inventory is at a five-year seasonal high. A South-East Asian extruder posting 25% revenue growth and its best quarter of the year says the weakness is not uniform across Asia - which is consistent with the trade-flow story on this board, where South-East Asia is being consolidated as the major supplementary scrap source by the UAE export ban and EU tariff increase. IT IS A SMALL COMPANY AND ONE QUARTER, SO IT IS WEIGHTED ACCORDINGLY: it is evidence that extrusion demand outside China is holding, not evidence that the global peak season has arrived.

earnings.note: H1-2026 interim results: alumina sales volume 1.296 Mt (+15.0% y/y from ~1.127 Mt) but average realised selling price USD 320/t against USD 529/t (-39.5%); revenue USD 415.0m (-30.5% y/y from USD 596.8m); gross profit USD 65.5m from USD 303.9m; gross margin 15.8% from 50.9%; profit attributable USD 62.7m (-74.8%); basic EPS USD 0.10 from USD 0.46; interim dividend cut to HKD 0.16 from HKD 0.65. Cash and equivalents more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings; total assets USD 2.496bn (+11.0%). THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. A 39.5% decline in realised ASP to USD 320/t, against a company-stated average international alumina price of about USD 307/t on an LME Platts basis versus about USD 447/t a year earlier, confirms from the seller's own accounts that the 2024-25 alumina squeeze has fully unwound. FOR THE METAL THIS IS MARGIN-POSITIVE AND PRICE-NEGATIVE, AND BOTH LEGS DESERVE EQUAL BILLING: non-integrated smelters buy alumina cheaper, but a lower cost curve lowers the price at which supply discipline would ever appear. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT IS THE CAPITAL: cash more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings, funding preparatory work on a 250,000 t/y Indonesian electrolytic aluminium first phase at about USD 436.6m over roughly two years with a further 500,000 t/y flagged medium term. Weak alumina prices are not slowing the ex-China metal capacity pipeline - they are being converted into it. Public disclosure only; no company-specific or confidential information is used or implied.

earnings.note: Revenue RMB 11.53bn, up 32.4% year on year. Net profit attributable to owners RMB 2.30bn, up 166.1%. EPS RMB 1.11 against RMB 0.58 in the corresponding period of last year, up 91.4%. THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

earnings.note: MARGINS EXPANDED SHARPLY WITH A THIRD OF THE VOLUME GONE. Adjusted net profit Dh2.46bn, up 34% year-on-year. Adjusted EBITDA Dh4.51bn, up 11% from Dh4.07bn, with the adjusted EBITDA margin widening to 33.3% from 27.0%. Revenue FELL 10% to Dh13.54bn from Dh15.08bn as aluminium sales dropped 32% to 939,000 t and cast metal production fell 29% to 1.01 Mt following the March incident at Al Taweelah. Reported net income Dh1.74bn after a Dh725m net incident impact. The company estimates around Dh1.5bn of capital expenditure to restore Al Taweelah, most of it in 2026, and guided cast metal back to pre-incident levels in Q1-2027 with the smelter at 25% of its reduction cells as of 26-Aug-2026 (315 of 1,262). THE COMPOSITION IS A PUBLIC CONFIRMATION OF THE MARGIN STRUCTURE THIS BOARD HAS DESCRIBED ALL CYCLE. Profit rose on three named drivers - higher realised aluminium prices, stronger regional premiums and LOWER ALUMINA PRICES - while a third of the sales volume was simply unavailable. A 630 basis-point margin expansion on a 10% revenue decline is only possible when the cost side has fallen faster than the top line, and the alumina leg is the reason. IT ALSO EXPLAINS TODAY'S PRICE ACTION IN ONE LINE: the same release that showed the margin also showed the recovery date, and the market traded the recovery date. The read-across to the alumina panel is direct - if Alunorte's 50% rate ends up lifting seaborne alumina, this is the margin that compresses first across the Gulf fleet.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

Q3-2026 guidance $325-345m. Liquidity $784.9m with cash $343.4m; cash exceeded total debt as of end-July after a $94.3m 2025 45X refund was received. Q2 adjustments included $61.3m for an Iceland equipment failure (net of tax) and $10.7m of Mt. Holly expansion cost. THE PUREST US AND SECTION-232 READ IN THE PEER SET, AND IT CONFIRMS THAT THE 2026 PRICE AND TARIFF STRUCTURE IS CONVERTING TO CASH. Adjusted EBITDA rose 41% sequentially on a 6.3% increase in shipments, which is operating leverage on price and premium rather than on volume. The last 90 Mt. Holly pots have been restarted, taking the plant to full capacity for the first time since 2015, and Grundartangi Line 2 is near full - so the volume base steps up again into Q3, which is why the guide moved higher despite Q2 already beating. That is the same message the input basket carries - a firming alumina and bauxite leg partly offsetting a falling energy leg - and it is the reason a rising LME does not translate one-for-one into producer margin.

earnings.note: BACK-FILLED INTO THE PER-COMPANY HISTORY PANEL THIS RUN WITH FOUR SOURCED QUARTERS OF ADJUSTED EBITDA. Q1 FY27 (three months to 30-June-2026): net income $164m, up 71% year on year; ADJUSTED EBITDA $516m, UP 24% year on year; adjusted EBITDA per tonne shipped $563, up 30% year on year; net sales $5.8bn. The prior three quarters were $459m in Q4 FY26 (down 3% y/y, $544/t), $348m in Q3 FY26 (down 5% y/y, $430/t) and $422m in Q2 FY26 (down 9% y/y, $448/t) - all three depressed by the Oswego fires of September and November 2025 and by tariff headwinds. THE FOUR-QUARTER SERIES IS THE POINT AND IT IS WHY THIS COMPANY WAS CHOSEN FOR THIS RUN'S BACKFILL: it is the cleanest public evidence available of how a downstream converter recovers from an operational shock, and of what the 2026 premium environment has been worth to the downstream. Adjusted EBITDA fell for three consecutive quarters - $422m, $348m, $459m - and then stepped up 12.4% sequentially and 24% year on year to $516m in the June quarter. THE PER-TONNE LINE IS THE MORE INFORMATIVE OF THE TWO because it strips shipment volume out: $448, $430, $544, $563. That is a 31% improvement in unit conversion economics across four quarters in a business whose metal cost is passed through. WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE IS AS IMPORTANT AS WHAT IT DOES: a converter's EBITDA per tonne rising through a period of record US premiums is consistent with the premium being captured downstream, but Novelis does not publish a split between recovered metal-price spread, recycling spread and true conversion pricing, so this page does not claim one. THE GENERIC READ-ACROSS IS THAT THE DOWNSTREAM SIDE OF THE CHAIN ENTERED THE SECOND HALF OF 2026 WITH MOMENTUM, which is consistent with Constellium and Kaiser on the same panel and with the stable $727.50 Rotterdam billet conversion spread on the premium panel.

OPERATIONALLY THE WEAKEST PRINT IN THE PEER SET: Q2 net finished production 155,469 t, DOWN 61% y/y, and sales volume 280,799 t, -32% y/y, with Lines 1, 2 and 3 still under controlled shutdown on regional tensions and raw-material availability. Value-added product was 195,891 t, 70% of shipments. THE SHARPEST ILLUSTRATION ON THIS BOARD OF WHAT THE 2026 MARKET IS ACTUALLY REWARDING: a producer can lose 61% of its output year-on-year and still nearly triple half-year profit, because average LME rose 46% y/y to $3,576/t in Q2. The company reported its highest-ever Q1 bauxite excavation at 19.52 lakh tonnes and its highest-ever Q1 calcined alumina production at 5.77 lakh tonnes. Added to this board and to the earnings-history panel this run as the designated progressive backfill. NALCO IS THE MOST FULLY INTEGRATED PRODUCER ON THIS PANEL - IT MINES ITS OWN BAUXITE, REFINES ITS OWN ALUMINA AND SMELTS - AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHY THIS PRINT IS USEFUL RATHER THAN JUST GOOD. A company that buys none of its alumina nearly doubling profit on record volumes tells you where margin is sitting in the chain: with whoever owns the alumina. Read directly against Chalco, the largest alumina producer in the world, whose Q2-2026 attributable profit fell 26.2% year on year in a quarter when the LME cash average was above $3,200 - the difference between the two is not the metal price, which both received, but scale, cost position and product mix. IT ALSO CUTS AGAINST THE ALUMINA-COST-SHOCK RISK THIS BOARD CARRIES: an integrated refiner posting record Q1 alumina output at 5.77 lakh tonnes is evidence of alumina availability rather than scarcity, and it sits on the same side of the argument as the alumina-to-aluminium ratio near 10.7-11.3%, well below the historical norm. THE HONEST QUALIFICATION: NALCO's exposure is predominantly Indian and its cost base is domestic coal-fired, so it is a weak read on seaborne alumina tightness, which is where this board locates the risk. Leverage was 1.8x at the quarter end. Management states that the 2028 targets of $900m ex-lag EBITDA and $300m of free cash flow will now be met two years early. THE METAL PRICE LAG IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR READING THIS PAGE and it is disclosed by the company: the $439m headline INCLUDES a $129m non-cash benefit from metal price lag, so the ex-lag figure is $310m. The four-quarter ex-lag path is $196m, $213m, $262m, $310m against headline figures of $235m, $280m, $359m and $439m - the gap between the two series has widened every quarter. THE READ-THROUGH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE ON THIS PANEL FOR ANYONE TRYING TO SIZE HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 EARNINGS CYCLE IS REAL. Constellium is a converter, not a smelter: it buys primary and scrap and sells rolled and extruded product, so a rising LME shows up in its results as a NON-CASH metal price lag benefit before it shows up anywhere in the operating business. That lag contributed $126m across the whole of FY2025 and $226m in the FIRST HALF of 2026 alone - it has nearly doubled in half the time. UNDERLYING PERFORMANCE IS GENUINELY GOOD, with ex-lag Adjusted EBITDA up 58% from $196m in Q3-2025 to $310m in Q2-2026 and the company pulling its 2028 targets forward by two years - but a reader who takes the $439m headline as operating performance overstates it by 29%. THE GENERAL POINT EXTENDS ACROSS THIS WHOLE PANEL: a large share of the 2026 aluminium earnings recovery is price-lag and inventory revaluation rather than volume or spread, which is exactly the kind of earnings that reverses when the LME stops rising - and the completed August board, on which aluminium's monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, is the first evidence that it may be about to.

earnings.note: ADDED TO THIS PANEL THIS RUN WITH A PRIMARY-SOURCED HISTORY TAKEN DIRECTLY FROM SEC FILINGS RATHER THAN FROM COVERAGE. Kaiser reported record Q2-2026 adjusted EBITDA of $166.3m against $67.7m a year earlier, a 146% increase, on net sales of $1.2566bn and conversion revenue of $437.0m. GAAP net income was $96.8m or $5.72 per diluted share against $23.2m and $1.41. Adjusted EBITDA margin on conversion revenue doubled to 38.1% from 18.1%. H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA was $294.8m against $141.1m. Net debt leverage improved to 2.1x from 3.4x at 31-December-2025 and the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised to +45-55% year on year from +20-30%. Shipments rose 6% to 305.7 million lbs, led by packaging at 155.8 million lbs and aerospace/high-strength at 60.8 million. THE READ-THROUGH IS A WARNING ABOUT HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 DOWNSTREAM EARNINGS CYCLE IS A PRICE ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEMAND ONE, AND KAISER DISCLOSES IT MORE HONESTLY THAN MOST. Adjusted EBITDA includes management-estimated FAVOURABLE METAL PRICE LAG of approximately $27.0m in Q2-2026 and $36.0m in Q1-2026 - $64.0m across the half against $36.0m in H1-2025. That is roughly 22% of H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA arising from the timing difference between the Midwest Transaction Price embedded in cost of sales and the market price over the period, not from conversion economics. MANAGEMENT SAID SO EXPLICITLY: the raised full-year outlook 'assumes a NEUTRAL metal price lag through the end of the year, and does not assume a continuation of the metal lag or consumption cost tailwinds recorded in the first half', and the CEO said the company expects aluminium price dynamics to normalise over the balance of the year. THE COMMERCIAL LESSON FOR READING THIS WHOLE PANEL: a rising aluminium price inflates downstream converter earnings twice - once through genuine mix and volume, once through inventory timing - and the second half reverses if the price stops rising. Kaiser's underlying story is nevertheless real: conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.43 from $1.30, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.12 from $0.92, and aerospace shipments grew as destocking eased. Both things are true at once and the filing quantifies the split, which is why this row is worth its place.

Dated reporting of 07-September-2026 has Iran saying an agreement with Oman to manage Strait of Hormuz shipping is days away, after more than three weeks of talks covering proposed inbound and outbound routes, the security and sovereignty of both states, and a proposed joint coordination centre; a separate 26-August report states a temporary maritime route had already been agreed. THE WATERWAY HAS NOT REOPENED: full reopening is reported as conditional on the United States fulfilling commitments under a June interim deal that has since lapsed, and no agreement is signed. THE ESCALATION FACTS ARE NOT DELETED - Iran said it attacked ten ships near the Strait and the United States said it sank five Iranian tankers. WHAT HAS CHANGED IS EVIDENTIAL CATEGORY, FROM UNCONFIRMED RUMOUR TO DATED MULTI-OUTLET REPORTING, AND THAT IS WHY THE CORRIDOR IS RE-RATED WHILE THE PHYSICAL POSITION IS NOT DECLARED REPAIRED. RE-RATED THIS RUN ON MATERIAL CHANGE. About 9% of global primary supply exits via the Strait of Hormuz and more than 80% of Gulf production is exported through it. THE CORRIDOR RE-ESCALATED OVER THE WEEKEND after a week in which this page had carried a de-escalation: US strikes on two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island on 30-August, Iranian retaliation against US bases, and an IRGC claim that a supertanker caught fire after striking naval mines. Brent rose 3.19% to $90.91 on it. President Trump stated on 01-September that strikes would be limited and the Strait is 'in very good condition' with large oil volumes moving; both statements are dated and both are carried. THE PHYSICAL POSITION BEHIND THE HEADLINES IS THE PART THAT HAS NOT CHANGED: Qatalum remains at roughly 60% of its 648 kt nameplate on reduced gas with no published restart timetable and a second Hydro force majeure outstanding; Alba has reduction Lines 1, 2 and 3 idled since March, 19% of 1,623 kt, with no announced restart and a stated intention to replace rather than restart them; EGA's Al Taweelah smelter is at 25% of cells with full production reaffirmed for Q1-2027. Gulf primary output ran roughly 40% below pre-war levels in April. This is the one corridor on the page where the disruption is both real and, in Qatalum's and Alba's cases, undated.

catalysts.text: TODAY'S LME OFFICIAL, DUE 13:20 LONDON, AND IT IS THE DIRECT TEST OF THIS PAGE'S LEAD FINDING. The question is not the flat price, it is whether the THREE-MONTH follows cash. Monday's session widened the backwardation from $24.00 to $54.00 with cash up 1.13% and three-month up only 0.22%. A SECOND SESSION OF WIDENING WITH FALLING STOCK WOULD CONFIRM A TIGHTENING TREND; A FLATTENING SPREAD WOULD SAY MONDAY WAS A ONE-SESSION PROMPT REQUIREMENT AND WOULD RETIRE THE FINDING. Watch the spread and the stock line, not the headline.

THE US 50% TARIFF ON ABOUT 100 CATEGORIES OF CANADIAN PRODUCTS TAKES EFFECT TODAY, with a vehicle and dairy import ban following on 29-September. Canada's 50% counter-tariffs have been in force since 08-September across $27.6bn of imports. The immediate read-through to primary aluminium is indirect, but a dated 14-September report already records auto-parts supply chains under pressure, and automotive is a top-two end-use for North American rolled and extruded metal.

FEDERAL RESERVE DECISION - THE SINGLE EVENT MOST LIKELY TO OVERWRITE EVERY READ ON THIS PAGE. Traders have increased bets on a rate HIKE after hot August US consumer prices, with the dollar index at 99.60 and the ten-year through 5%. A hike, or a hawkish hold, strengthens the dollar headwind that aluminium advanced INTO on Monday. Note the offsetting second-order effect: higher funding costs raise the carrying cost of financed inventory, which supports a backwardated front even as it pressures flat price.

MONTHLY SETTLEMENT WINDOW FOR THE CARBON INPUTS - PREBAKED ANODES, COAL TAR PITCH AND THE GREEN PETROLEUM COKE FEEDSTOCK. These rows settle on a monthly cycle around the 17th-18th and are the next scheduled opportunity for the smelter input basket to move on anything other than the daily copper mark. Anodes are 13-16% of cash cost and pitch 2-3%, so an anode settlement matters roughly five times more than a pitch one.

THE JAPANESE Q4 QUARTERLY PREMIUM SETTLEMENT. Producer offers are $310-325/t against a settled Q3 record of $395/t, with market consensus at $280-290/t. The gap between offer and consensus is the negotiation, and the consensus sitting below the offer puts the burden of concession on sellers. A settlement at $285 would be a roughly 28% single-quarter fall and would reset Asian realisations for the whole of Q4.

ALUMINIUM 2026, DUSSELDORF - the industry's largest trade exhibition, and historically a window in which producers, traders and consumers make public statements about regional availability and contract terms for the following year. Public commentary from that event is the most likely source of a dated premium or availability mark outside the normal assessment cycle.

risks.text: TARIFF POLICY, NOT SUPPLY AND DEMAND, REMAINS THE DOMINANT DETERMINANT OF REGIONAL DELIVERED PRICE - AND A PRODUCER PUT NUMBERS ON IT THIS RUN. Re-assessed 15-September and HELD AT UP. Section 232 at 50% is levied on value, so the 14-September cash rise of $37.00 mechanically added $18.50 to the tariff leg of every US duty-paid tonne with nothing physical behind it; the leg now stands at $1,655.50 against a newly sourced delivered level of about $2,403/t, leaving an implied market leg of roughly $747.50 - about 31% of the premium. WHAT IS NEW AND DATED: Alcoa's CFO stated publicly on 14-September that a Canada-only tariff cut would NOT bring the Midwest premium down significantly, because the US must import about 4 Mt/y against roughly 3 Mt of Canadian capability. The US 50% tariff on about 100 categories of Canadian products takes effect today, 15-September, with a vehicle and dairy import ban following 29-September, and Canada's 50% counter-tariffs have been in force since 08-September across $27.6bn of imports. A dated 14-September report records the dispute pressuring North American auto-parts supply chains. THE RISK IS ESCALATING ON A PUBLISHED SCHEDULE, WHICH IS WHY THE TREND STAYS UP.

A FEDERAL RESERVE RATE HIKE ON WEDNESDAY 16-SEPTEMBER WOULD REMOVE THE MONETARY LEG FROM EVERY INDUSTRIAL-METAL BULL CASE AT THE MOMENT THE PHYSICAL MARKET IS TIGHTENING. RAISED TO UP THIS RUN, DELIBERATELY AND ON DATED EVIDENCE. The commodity reference board records that traders have INCREASED bets on a rate HIKE after hot August US consumer prices; the dollar index is 99.60 and firming, the US ten-year is through 5% at 5.013%, and the LME euro fixing fell 0.38% to 1.15480 on the 14-September board. NOTE THE SECOND-ORDER EFFECT THAT CUTS THE OTHER WAY AND IS NOT SUPPRESSED: a yield above 5% raises the carrying cost of financed inventory, which discourages holding metal off-warrant and therefore supports a backwardated front. THE NET IS STILL NEGATIVE FOR FLAT PRICE AND THE EVENT IS 24 HOURS AWAY, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS THE HIGHEST-URGENCY ROW ON THE REGISTER TODAY.

THE ASIAN QUARTERLY PREMIUM SETTLES 18-28% BELOW THE Q3 RECORD AND RESETS REGIONAL REALISATIONS ACROSS THE WHOLE OF Q4. HELD AT UP ON UNCHANGED EVIDENCE. Producer offers for October-December shipments are reported at $310-325/t against a settled Q3 of $395/t, while a separate market consensus puts the likely outcome at $280-290/t, with Korean and Thai traders repricing toward that band. The consensus sits BELOW the producers' own opening offer, which puts the burden of concession on the sellers. A settlement at $285 would be a fall of roughly 28% in a single quarter. THE TENSION WITH THE 14-SEPTEMBER LME BOARD IS REAL AND IS LEFT UNRESOLVED RATHER THAN EXPLAINED AWAY: warrant metal in a warehouse tightened sharply while delivered metal into Japan is being negotiated sharply lower. Those are different products in different places and they are allowed to disagree.

THE GULF SUPPLY DISRUPTION REPAIRS FASTER THAN THE MARKET EXPECTS, REMOVING THE SCARCITY PILLAR UNDER WESTERN PREMIUMS. LOWERED TO FLAT THIS RUN AND THE CHANGE IS DELIBERATE. For a week this row trended up on dated SMM commentary that damaged Middle East capacity was recovering. A dated 14-September public disclosure from a listed producer cuts directly against it: Middle East supply 'has been constrained by the war', North American and European customers are actively seeking material, and the producer's order book is almost completely sold out for the remainder of 2026. TWO CREDIBLE DATED SOURCES NOW DISAGREE ABOUT THE SAME FACT, AND THE HONEST RESPONSE TO A GENUINE EVIDENTIAL CONFLICT IS TO SET THE TREND TO FLAT RATHER THAN PICK A WINNER. Restart trackers on the producer panel remain the arbiter and none has published a new disclosure.

THE CAPACITY PIPELINE DELIVERS INTO A MARKET THAT NO LONGER NEEDS IT, CLOSING THE UNUSUALLY WIDE CONVERSION MARGINS THE PEER PANEL HAS BEEN REPORTING. HELD AT UP. Two dated 14-September items extend the pipeline: Rusal is nearing final permitting for a bauxite-to-alumina project in Kalimantan, Indonesia, and Mercuria and Glencore are exploring a deal for Venezuela's Venalum smelter. These sit alongside the Saudi 500 kt/y integrated greenfield under construction, the Slovalco restart, Magnitude 7's first potline guided before end-2026 and Century's Mt Holly return to full capacity. NEITHER NEW ITEM CHANGES A 2026 BALANCE AND NEITHER IS PRESENTED AS IF IT DOES - refineries and smelter restarts run on multi-year clocks - but the pipeline is visibly lengthening in exactly the regions where energy is cheap, and that is what eventually closes a margin this wide.

THE ENERGY AND SUPPLY-ROUTE SHOCK RE-ACCELERATES, RE-INFLATING THE SMELTER COST BASE AND THE FREIGHT BILL TOGETHER. LOWERED TO DOWN THIS RUN ON THE DAY'S PRICE EVIDENCE, WITH THE UNDERLYING RISK EXPLICITLY UNRESOLVED. Brent rose 1.21% against 2.86% the previous session and sits below the level this page carried yesterday; European gas actually EASED 0.33% to about EUR 82.30/MWh after jumping 4.56%. The gas leg is the commercially important one because power is 30-40% of primary cash cost and European marginal power is gas-set. THE CAUSES HAVE NOT GONE AWAY: the Hormuz corridor talks remain postponed and the Saudi East-West bypass pipeline remains shut with no restart date published. THE TREND IS LOWERED ON PRICE ACTION, NOT ON A RESOLUTION, AND THAT DISTINCTION IS THE POINT - a single session of deceleration is not a de-escalation and will be reversed on this register the moment the prices say so.

THE THREE-MONTH FAILS TO FOLLOW CASH AND THE BACKWARDATION FLATTENS BACK, REVEALING THE 14-SEPTEMBER MOVE AS A ONE-SESSION SQUEEZE RATHER THAN A TIGHTENING TREND. NEW ROW THIS RUN, ADDED BECAUSE IT IS THE SPECIFIC WAY THIS PAGE'S LEAD FINDING COULD BE WRONG AND IT DESERVES TO BE VISIBLE. Three-month rose only $7.00 against cash's $37.00 and remains $4.00 below the 3,261 pivot it lost on Friday. A backwardation that widens without the forward curve following is as consistent with a short squeeze or a single large prompt requirement as it is with a durable shortage, AND THIS PAGE CANNOT DISTINGUISH BETWEEN THOSE TWO FROM PUBLIC DATA ALONE. The test is repetition: a second and third session of widening spread with falling stock would settle it; a flattening spread today would retire the finding. TREND SET TO FLAT RATHER THAN DOWN BECAUSE THE STOCK LINE IS CORROBORATING THE SPREAD SO FAR.

DOWNSTREAM DEMAND DESTRUCTION FROM SUSTAINED TRADE FRICTION FEEDS BACK INTO PRIMARY ORDER BOOKS. HELD AT UP. A dated 14-September report records the US-Canada dispute pressuring North American auto-parts supply chains, with parts makers facing higher costs and uncertainty over where components should be produced across a network built over decades. A dated 15-September report records a British Columbia extruder publicly refusing to relocate to the US despite tariffs threatening more than 40% of its sales. AUTOMOTIVE IS ONE OF THE LARGEST END-USES FOR BOTH ROLLED AND EXTRUDED ALUMINIUM IN NORTH AMERICA, and prolonged sourcing uncertainty is a brake on order books regardless of where the metal is priced. This is the slowest-moving row on the register and the one most likely to be under-weighted by a page that watches exchange prices daily.

balance.label: Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED AND THE 11-SEPTEMBER DATA SHARPENS THE CENTRAL PUZZLE RATHER THAN RESOLVING IT: global primary production was reported down 1.7% year on year at 6.16 million tonnes and GCC output down 44% year on year in July to 293,000 tonnes from 523,000 - a genuine, large supply loss. YET China's August exports were 626,000 tonnes, taking January-August to 4.67 million tonnes, up 16.7% year on year, and dated commentary describes Middle Eastern and Australian ingot supply into Japan as RELATIVELY AMPLE with Asian premiums collapsing toward a $280-290 Q4 consensus. A DEFICIT IN PRIMARY UNITS CAN COEXIST WITH AMPLE REGIONAL AVAILABILITY IF THE RELIEVING METAL ARRIVES AS CHINESE SEMI-FINISHED AND ALLOY PRODUCT THAT NEVER PASSES THROUGH AN LME WAREHOUSE - which is the most coherent published explanation for why a multi-decade exchange inventory low, a widening backwardation and collapsing physical premiums are all true at once.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.
